title: Deep Holes in the Clifford Hierarchy
abstract: We determine the covering radius of the topological closure of the single-qubit Clifford hierarchy in $\SU(2)\cong S^3$. This closure is a union of $18$ great circles --- the Clifford--Pauli circles --- and we prove that its covering radius is $\arccos\sqrt{5/6}$. The extremal points, which we call \emph{deep holes}, form a single orbit of size $192$ under left and right multiplication by Clifford gates, and are described in closed form. Equivalently, the minimum over one-qubit unitaries of the all-level Clifford fidelity is $5/6$. The proof rests on two structures attached to the configuration of $18$ planes in $\R^4$: their centered rank-two projectors form an orthonormal basis of the irreducible $\SO(4)$-module $\Sym_0(4)$, and the projection profile of a unit quaternion is exactly its image under the double cover $\SU(2)\to\SO(3)$. These reduce the covering problem to a minimax statement for the $\ell^\infty$-norm on $\SO(3)$ which we solve exactly, classifying its equality cases.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the covering radius associated with the single-qubit Clifford gate set embedded in SU(2). By mapping the problem onto a minimization task on SO(3), the authors precisely determine this radius to be arccos(sqrt(5)/6). This result quantifies a fundamental geometric limit on the fidelity achievable by sequences of Clifford gates.
main_problem: The paper determines the covering radius of the topological closure of the single-qubit Clifford hierarchy within SU(2) (identified with S^3). This is equivalent to finding the minimum all-level Clifford fidelity.
main_result: The covering radius is found to be arccos(sqrt(5)/6), and the extremal points, called 'deep holes', form a single orbit of size 192 under Clifford gate multiplication.
method: The problem is solved by mapping the geometry from S^3 to SO(3) via a quaternionic double cover. This reduces the covering problem to an exact minimax statement concerning the L-infinity norm on SO(3).
model_or_system: The system models the single-qubit quantum gate space, represented by SU(2) or S^3. The structure analyzed is the closure of the Clifford hierarchy, which forms a union of 18 great circles in this space.

paper_structure: The paper first defines the geometry (18 circles in S^3) and establishes an orthonormal basis for their projectors. It then maps the covering problem from S^3 to a minimax statement on SO(3), solving this final geometric minimization problem.
why_interesting: This work provides deep mathematical insights into the fundamental structure of quantum gate sets, which is crucial for understanding universal quantum computation and resource estimation in quantum information theory.
